newsitem.title: PERU: Popularity of Peru's Fujimori plunges - polls.
newsitem.headline: Popularity of Peru's Fujimori plunges - polls.

text.p: The popularity of Peru's President Alberto Fujimori, shaken by a four-month long hostage crisis and scandals in the security forces, has plummeted to almost historic lows, according to opinion polls published on Sunday.
One survey, by local pollsters Analistas y Consultores, showed that just 35 percent of those questioned in April approved of Fujimori, down sharply from 42.5 percent in March.

Disapproval of Fujimori rose to 52 percent, from 44.3 percent in March, according to the poll of 400 people which was carried by the Frecuencia Latina television network. The poll had a 4.9 percent margin of error.
Fujimori, who was comfortably re-elected to a second five year term in July 1995, has been beset by political problems in recent weeks.

Failure to persuade Marxist rebels to release 72 Peruvian and Japanese VIPs held for 123 days has been joined by accusations of torture by army intelligence agents and persistent criticisms of close aide and security adviser Vladimir Montesinos.
A separate survey, by local polling firm Imasen, showed Fujimori's popularity plunging 11 percentage points to 43.8 percent between March and April.
"This is the second lowest level of approval ever for Fujimori," Imasen director Giovana Penaflor, was quoted as saying by La Republica newspaper which published the poll of 402 people.

Fujimori's approval rating fell to 41 percent in Imasen polls in December 1996 after the brief kidnapping and arrest by the army intelligence service of retired army Gen. Rodolfo Robles for allegedly insulting the armed forces.
